name: Question 1
problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q(\sqrt{3},\,\frac{11}{2},\,-7)$ and parallel to $v=⟨1,\,1,\,-2⟩.$
worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $Q$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=q+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$ 

In our case, the position vector of the point $Q$ is $q=⟨\sqrt{3},\,\frac{11}{2},\,-7⟩.$ 

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
r=⟨\sqrt{3},\,\frac{11}{2},\,-7⟩+t⟨1,\,1,\,-2⟩,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Question 1
?

Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through Q(3,112,−7) and parallel to v=⟨1,1,−2⟩.

a
r=⟨1,1,−2⟩+⟨−7,112,3⟩
b
r=⟨112,3,−7⟩+t⟨−1,1,−2⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=⟨1,1,−2⟩+t⟨−7,112,3⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=⟨1,1,−2⟩+t⟨3,112,−7⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=⟨3,112,−7⟩+t⟨1,1,−2⟩,t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The vector equation of the straight line passing through Q and parallel to v is given by r=q+tv,

where t∈(−∞,∞) and q is the position vector of Q.

In our case, the position vector of the point Q is q=⟨3,112,−7⟩.

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

r=⟨3,112,−7⟩+t⟨1,1,−2⟩,t∈(−∞,∞).
